The `save_*()` functions put results in the right `outputs/` folder and record each one
in `framework.db`, so `result_list()` can show what the project has produced.

```{python}
#| label: setup
import framework as fw
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

root = fw.scaffold()
bp = fw.data_read("inputs.final.bp_analysis")
```

## Tables

A table of mean systolic and diastolic pressure by arm and visit.

```{python}
table = (
    bp.groupby(["treatment", "visit_number"])
    .agg(n=("systolic_bp", "size"),
         systolic=("systolic_bp", "mean"),
         diastolic=("diastolic_bp", "mean"))
    .round(1)
    .reset_index()
)
table
```

`save_table()` writes CSV by default and returns the path. Look for the new
`outputs/tables/` folder in the messages.

```{python}
fw.save_table(table, "bp_by_visit")
```

Parquet keeps the column types. (`format="xlsx"` needs the `excel` extra.)

```{python}
fw.save_table(table, "bp_by_visit", format="parquet")
```

A name with a slash saves into a subfolder, which is created.

```{python}
fw.save_table(table, "meeting-2026-11/bp_by_visit")
```

`show_table()` shows a table in the page the way `knitr::kable()` does in R: a Markdown
table that Quarto styles like the rest of the page. `digits` fixes the decimals.

```{python}
fw.show_table(table, caption="Mean blood pressure by arm and visit", digits=1)
```

## Figures

Mean systolic pressure over visits, one line per arm.

```{python}
means = bp.groupby(["visit_number", "treatment"])["systolic_bp"].mean().unstack()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
for arm, color in (("control", "#7a7a7a"), ("intervention", "#1f6fb2")):
    ax.plot(means.index, means[arm], marker="o", color=color, label=arm)
ax.set(xlabel="Visit", ylabel="Mean systolic BP (mmHg)", xticks=means.index,
       title="Systolic blood pressure by visit")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
plt.show()
```

`save_figure()` takes a matplotlib figure (or an Axes, a seaborn grid, a plotnine plot,
or `None` for the current figure). Width and height are in inches.

```{python}
fw.save_figure(fig, "bp_trend", width=6, height=4)
```

A list of formats saves one file per format, and a name with a slash saves into a
subfolder. Look at the three paths it returns.

```{python}
fw.save_figure(fig, "meeting-2026-11/bp_trend", format=["png", "svg", "pdf"],
               width=6, height=4)
```

## Models

An ordinary least squares model of systolic pressure on visit, arm, and their
interaction, adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and smoking.

```{python}
model = smf.ols(
    "systolic_bp ~ visit_number * treatment + age + sex + bmi + smoker", data=bp
).fit()
model.params.round(2)
```

`save_model()` pickles any fitted model to `outputs/models/<name>.pkl`.

```{python}
fw.save_model(model, "bp_ols")
```

`load_model()` loads it back by name, as a working results object. It warns if the
file changed since it was saved. (Loading is pickle's, so only load models from projects
you trust.)

```{python}
reloaded = fw.load_model("bp_ols")
round(float(reloaded.rsquared), 3)
```

## Rendered notebooks

`save_notebook()` renders a `.qmd` or `.ipynb` with Quarto and saves the HTML in
`outputs/notebooks/`. This renders the short `bp-brief.qmd` beside this notebook.
It takes a few seconds.

```{python}
fw.save_notebook(root / "notebooks" / "bp-brief.qmd", name="bp-brief")
```

## Reports

`save_report()` copies a finished file into `outputs/reports/`. Here a short Markdown
summary is written to scratch first, then saved as a report.

```{python}
interaction = model.params["visit_number:treatment[T.intervention]"]
low, high = model.conf_int().loc["visit_number:treatment[T.intervention]"]

draft = root / fw.settings("scratch") / "bp-summary.md"
draft.write_text(
    "# Blood pressure summary\n\n"
    f"Across {bp['participant_id'].nunique()} participants and {len(bp)} visits, "
    f"systolic pressure in the intervention arm fell {abs(interaction):.1f} mmHg more "
    f"per visit than in control (95% CI {low:.1f} to {high:.1f}).\n"
)
fw.save_report(draft, name="bp-summary")
```

## Listing results

`result_list()` shows everything saved, newest first, with a hash of each file.

```{python}
fw.result_list()[["name", "type", "public", "created_at"]]
```

Filter by type.

```{python}
fw.result_list(type="figure")[["name", "updated_at"]]
```

## Scratch

`scratch_capture()` writes an object to `scratch/` for a quick look and returns it
unchanged, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline. DataFrames become TSV.

```{python}
top = fw.scratch_capture(
    bp.sort_values("systolic_bp", ascending=False), name="highest_bp.tsv", n=20
)
len(top)
```

Other objects become text, or pickle with `to="pickle"`.

```{python}
fw.scratch_capture(model.summary(), name="bp_ols_summary.txt")
sorted(p.name for p in (root / fw.settings("scratch")).iterdir())
```

`scratch_clean()` deletes the files in `scratch/` (git ignores the folder anyway).

```{python}
fw.scratch_clean()
sorted(p.name for p in (root / fw.settings("scratch")).iterdir())
```
